owner_rules: Done means ALL evidence: implemented as specified (task id), a test that FAILED before and passes now, suites green, measured number vs target, docs regenerated, committed AND pushed to the contract's branch.
Never defer: no "later", "follow-up", "out of scope". If blocked: what blocks, what you tried, what you need; then continue with the next task.
Root cause, then fix: file:line + mechanism. No weakening tests, raising timeouts, skips, relaxed assertions.
No silent scope cuts: never lower targets, caps or test sizes without owner approval.

Deliver continuously: one task per commit, pushed to the contract's branch as it goes green.
Honest reporting: TASK-ID | status | commit | tests | measured vs target | missing.

title: SR-1.35 Memev is fast on every axis we measured
request:
Owner, 6 Nov 2026, verbatim: "implement all the speed enhancements, set up a contract to speed up every axis you identified, using arxiv research, and [two protocol files, paths left out] to find candidates and new spliced protocols we invent, 5 per axis and test on test rig, fons speed up as fast as possible 3 iteration loops". Then: "when all of this lands it is ?0 get everything fixed and wired in , and then retest and publish results on repo". Then: "memory speed and metrics should be available in the rev2 memory tab as health".

Scope of speed: wall time and thread blocking on the user's machine. Hosted services, the paid engine and the native app are out of scope.

This contract is signed after its code landed, with its base at 93d97329a9257c6e4d03a1f1ff4650abd998845c, the commit before that code, so its red runs are honest. The code landed by PR 437 at 5a611af1a1f949889d8623d24ab8067f870ad95e, on the owner's word to integrate. It was built before this contract was written, against a draft of it: that is the order the owner's priority set, and it is said here rather than hidden. PR 439 and PR 440 followed it with tests and the ceilings' guard list. The red runs were read off a run of the new tests on main's code, and the criteria claim a red run only where a test failed by assertion.

Version 2, 7 Nov 2026, supersedes the owner's signature of 6 Nov on version 1 (contract k-sr-1-35-memev-is-fast-on-017214, at 1b58023196e565bdbf2b26e9713b74c77f8c2e28). Version 1 could not pass as signed: its full-suite command sets MEMEV_NO_SERVICE, and three tests in test/service-windows.test.mjs failed under it on every machine, which CI never showed because CI does not set it; the engine also cut version 1's request at 4,000 characters without a word. Both are fixed on main before this version: PR 447 for the test, PR 446 so a draft refuses an over-long request and the owner's route compares the drafted request with the spec. The same range also moves one ceiling: on a 16-core Linux server main's code imports 50,000 notes in 60,601 ms against a ceiling of 200,000, so a7_first_import_ms is a guard and seven ceilings catch the old code (PR 448, docs/testing/SPEED-RESULTS.md). A full rehearsal through the real verifier on the Linux server then found three more things, all fixed before this version: a test with a fixed date that failed from 7 Nov (PR 449), the ceilings' vault holding no git identity of its own (PR 450), a scope drawn from a diff of the end points when the verifier walks every commit, and a vault's seeded bus folder read as uncommitted (PR 451, the owner's merge). The base stays the commit before the code, so the red runs stay honest, and the scope holds everything landed since it, including version 1's signed body.

Version 3, 7 Nov 2026, supersedes the owner's signature of 7 Nov on version 2 (contract k-sr-1-35-memev-is-fast-on-ccc1fc, merged at a033aa22305ec5f005d3e2e2157587367f64a7db). Version 2 could not pass as signed. A rehearsal of the real verifier at a later commit found two causes, both in T1-c00. First, the owner merged version 2 in the web UI with GitHub's default subject, which names the owner's account, and the leak scan flags that word; the file that fixes it, scripts/leak-scan.mjs, was outside version 2's scope, so the scope criterion failed on every task. Second, test/hooks-startup.test.mjs compared SR-1.29's hook start-up against MEMEV_CONTRACT_BASE. Here that base already holds SR-1.29's change, so the ratio was about 1 against a 0.7 bar on every run. Earlier rehearsals missed it because their reruns did not set that variable; a rerun now uses the verifier's own environment, base included. PR 453 fixes both before this version. The leak scan accepts that subject only when the name in it is the owner in the origin remote's GitHub URL for memev; with any other origin it accepts nothing. The origin is the clone's own configuration, so it decides only what that clone accepts in its own history; CI and the verify clone take it from GitHub. The start-up comparison builds SR-1.29's own base, read from its spec. The scope adds scripts/leak-scan.mjs, test/leak-scan.test.mjs, test/hooks-startup.test.mjs and changelog.d/sr-1-35-v3-gates.md to every task. A later contract that changes hook output on purpose must change test/hooks-startup.test.mjs as well, so it needs that file in its scope. The 70 percent start-up bar moves with a warm cache and with a loader on one side (contracts/seed-readiness/AMENDMENTS.md); the rehearsal of this version records the ratio it saw.

Scope. Because the base is before the code, the range from the base to the head also holds the pull request that lands this contract, so the scope names the contract's own files: its spec, record, snapshot, signed body, the manifest, the contracts README and the WBS. Any later commit to main falls in the same range and fails the scope criterion on a later verify, so the first verify after signing is the one that counts.

Rules for every axis. R4: a speed gain never changes behaviour; answers match the real index on the oracle prompts, every durability and detection promise stays, and each change's own test fails before it. R5: no skipped tests, raised timeouts or relaxed assertions; a test of a replaced file format may be rewritten to test the same promise, and says so. R6: a claim needs a number from committed code on a named commit, an effect beyond run-to-run spread, and a kill attempt by an agent that did not build it.

Review. An agent that did not build it made a kill attempt, and found the code not safe: three high and six medium findings, among them damage to the index going unnoticed. The fixes were attacked by the second seat three times, on the same machine, and each time more was found and fixed. Both seats are AI on one machine, so this is not independent review. The attempt and the attacks did not cover power loss, a real vault at scale, two computers through git, or Windows.

Measured on one iMac at 50,000 generated notes, main's code against this code: start 44.8 s and 1.08 s; first import 374 s and 74 s; recall p95 135 to 157 ms and 16 to 33 ms; first recall after a save 7.2 to 9.5 s and 18 to 26 ms; /healthz timeouts while writing 8 per cycle and 0; the thread blocked by a commit 215 ms and 0.5 ms; bus roster at 100,000 messages 2,904 ms and 3.5 ms. Append and the first bus read show no gain beyond the spread, and none is claimed. Those figures were taken at 5355c9a4b896cef443c9d715a6ada5f22cf5b584; the later commits change the commit catch-up after a hard kill and add the bench, so only A5 can feel them, and the ceilings run at 79a712d3 re-measured A5 at 0.5 ms.

Second seat. The owner waived the second seat for this work while it was stopped, in his word "wave for this". It has since returned and reviews this contract all the same.

Stated limit, chosen and not an oversight: going back to code older than rotation, after a bus file has rolled over, can reuse counters and leave a new message undelivered. The layout that avoided this lost messages to a reader in another process in normal use, so it was removed. No tag, release or package of the older code exists.

Known and not here: two processes writing at once fail the log's verify, on main too; SR-1.01's writer lock closes that, and SR-0.04 T3 lands it after this. A kill before the first commit leaves a bus message uncommitted until the next commit. Damage checks catch damage and not a forger who recomputes them.
